cohort: 220 mothers receiving care at the Women's Health Training and Research Hospital in Ankara, Turkey between February 10 and August 10, 2016
finding: Breastfeeding success was associated with previous and current breastfeeding problems, maternal age, and prior breastfeeding experience.
mod_finding: Newborns without complications should be placed in skin-to-skin contact (SSC) with their mothers immediately after cesarean section, breastfed within the first hour after birth, and remain in SSC until the end of the first breastfeeding to increase breastfeeding success.
